desc: Titled "The 2026 Personal Brand Audit — 5 Queries to Run Right Now." Five query templates in a numbered vertical list with instructions: (1) "Tell me about [your name]" — check accuracy; (2) "What is [your name] known for?" — check completeness; (3) "Best [your profession] in [city]?" — check category appearance; (4) "What is [your name]'s methodology?" — check knowledge depth; (5) "Who is similar to [your name]?" — check comparative positioning. Score guide: 5/5 accurate and present = strong machine-readable brand. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The 30-Minute AI Presence Self-Audit." Five steps in a numbered vertical flow, each with a time allocation and a "What to look for" line: (1) AI Platform Testing — 10 min — Do you appear in ChatGPT and Perplexity queries?; (2) GBP Check — 5 min — Is your profile claimed, current, and consistent?; (3) NAP Consistency — 5 min — Is your name/address/phone identical everywhere?; (4) Schema Markup — 5 min — Does Google's Rich Results Test show LocalBusiness schema?; (5) Content Citability — 5 min — Does your site have any page AI can quote? Scoring guide at bottom: 4–5 passes = strong foundation; 2–3 passes = significant gaps; 0–1 passes = urgent action needed. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The Missed Call Problem — By the Numbers." Five data-point callouts in a vertical layout: (1) 62% of small business calls go unanswered; (2) 85% of missed callers never call back; (3) $126,000 average annual revenue lost per business; (4) 30–40% of missed calls happen after hours; (5) 85% of homeowners hire the first contractor who responds. Bottom callout: "This is not a marketing problem. It is an intake infrastructure problem." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SEO vs. AEO vs. GEO: What Each One Targets." Three-column layout. Column 1 (SEO): Target = Google organic results; Key factors = keywords, backlinks, domain authority; Who's doing it = most businesses. Column 2 (AEO): Target = Featured snippets, People Also Ask; Key factors = FAQ structure, direct answers; Who's doing it = few small businesses. Column 3 (GEO): Target = ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews; Key factors = schema, citations, entity clarity; Who's doing it = fewer than 12% of marketing teams. Bold callout at bottom: "Most businesses are optimizing for one surface. Customers are using all three." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "AI Search vs Traditional Search — How Discovery Works in 2026." Two-column comparison. TRADITIONAL SEARCH: ranking model, 10 links returned, keyword + authority signals, 60%+ end without click, dominant volume channel. AI SEARCH: synthesis model, 2-3 businesses named, schema + entity + citation signals, converts at 4.4× organic rate, growing at +600% YoY. Bottom: "Both channels are active. Both require different infrastructure. Most businesses are only optimizing for one." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Why CPA Firms Are Invisible to AI — and What to Fix First." Five rows: (1) No FAQ content — AI has nothing to cite; (2) GBP unclaimed — invisible in local search; (3) Credentials not machine-readable — schema missing; (4) Directory presence incomplete — no third-party authority signals; (5) Zero AI-specific content strategy — fewer than 12% of professional service firms have one. Each row has a fix note. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Traffic vs AI Visibility — What Each Metric Captures." Two-column comparison. TRAFFIC METRICS: sessions, pageviews, bounce rate, referral source — measures who arrived. AI VISIBILITY METRICS: citation rate, description accuracy, category presence, platform breadth — measures whether you're being discovered. Bold callout: "AI-referred visitors convert at 4.4× the rate of organic search visitors. Traffic dashboards barely register them." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "AI Voice Agent vs Live Receptionist — 2026 Cost and Capability Comparison." Table with five comparison dimensions. Bold callout: "Small businesses lose $126,000/year from missed calls. An AI voice agent costs $249/month and answers every call on the first ring, 24/7." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The AICC Verification Framework — How SX Audits Assesses AI Presence." Four-section breakdown with description of each dimension and what it checks. AI Readiness Score composite shown at bottom. Bold callout: "Most AI visibility checks are single-platform and unstructured. AICC measures Accuracy, Identity Consistency, Citability, and Cross-Platform Coverage." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What a Website Needs to Actually Work in 2026." Two columns. LEFT: "What Most Designers Deliver" — professional design, fast hosting, mobile layout, contact form. RIGHT: "What Drives Discovery" — LocalBusiness schema markup, FAQ / structured content, consistent NAP with GBP, original content AI can cite, sub-3-second mobile load. Bold callout: "Design determines whether they stay. Infrastructure determines whether they arrive." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Rented vs. Owned Digital Infrastructure." Two-column comparison. RENTED: Instagram (algorithm controls reach), Facebook (organic reach ~2%), TikTok (content restrictions applied without warning), GBP (can be suspended), Yelp (platform manages listing). OWNED: Website (full control), Email list (no algorithm), Direct booking (platform-independent), Blog content (compounds over time). Bold callout: "Businesses with owned infrastructure generate 2× more revenue than those with social-only presence." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Owned vs. Rented Digital Channels — What Small Businesses Are Building On." Two columns. LEFT: "Rented" — Instagram (platform controls reach), Facebook (organic reach: ~2%), GBP (can be suspended without warning), Yelp (platform manages your listing), App marketplaces (rules change unilaterally). RIGHT: "Owned" — Website (you control it), Email list (no algorithm between you and your audience), Direct booking (zero platform dependency), Blog content (compounds over time). Bold callout: "90% of local businesses rely primarily on rented channels." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Why Your Contractor Website Isn't Producing Calls." Five-finding layout with dollar impact callouts: (1) GBP unclaimed or incomplete — 70% of leads come from GBP; (2) Response time over 1 hour — 3.5× lower conversion rate; (3) Invisible to AI search — 37% of homeowner research starts on ChatGPT/Perplexity; (4) No service-area or FAQ content — zero citation targets for AI; (5) No after-hours capture — evening inquiries 100% lost. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The Four-Layer New-Patient Visibility Framework for Dental Practices." Four horizontal bars stacked, each representing a layer: Foundation → Visibility → AI Presence → Conversion. Each bar lists three to four key components. A funnel visual at the right shows new patients entering at the top and dropping off at each layer with poor infrastructure. Bottom callout: "93% of patients search online before booking. Most practices only capture a fraction of them." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Why Digital Marketing Fails Without Prior Diagnosis." Two-path diagram. PATH A (No Diagnosis): New website → Content calendar → Ads → 8 months → Marginal results → Foundation still broken. PATH B (Diagnosis First): Audit → Fix foundation (NAP, schema, GBP, trust) → Implement on solid base → Results compound. Below both paths: "The difference between the paths is not budget. It's sequence." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Known vs. Findable vs. AI-Discoverable — What Each Layer Means for Growth." Three rows: KNOWN (how it works: referral network and word of mouth; reach: limited to existing network; growth ceiling: yes); FINDABLE (how it works: Google search and Maps; reach: anyone actively searching your category; growth ceiling: lower); AI-DISCOVERABLE (how it works: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews; reach: high-intent searchers using AI for recommendations; conversion rate: 4.4× traditional search). Bold callout: "Only 4.3% of businesses are AI-discoverable for exploratory queries. That is the competitive gap." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Digital Audit vs Marketing Audit — What Each Covers and Which Comes First." Two-column layout. DIGITAL AUDIT: website technical health, schema markup, GBP status, NAP consistency, AI visibility, trust signals — answers: "Is the infrastructure working?" MARKETING AUDIT: channel performance, content strategy, conversion paths, messaging alignment, ROI by channel — answers: "Is the strategy working?" Arrow below: "Digital audit first → Marketing audit second. This is the sequence that produces results." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What Your Digital First Impression Is Actually Saying." Five-point audit checklist with status indicators: Website design and currency, GBP completeness and reviews, Consistency across platforms, AI summary accuracy, Response to negative content. Each point marked: BUILDING TRUST / NEUTRAL / RAISING DOUBT. Bottom callout: "97% of consumers research businesses online before any purchase decision. The digital impression happens before you ever speak." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Digital Sovereignty Stack — What Small Business Actually Owns." Three-tier vertical diagram. FOUNDATION (owned): website with schema markup, email list, direct booking system. VISIBILITY (rented but essential): GBP, NAP directories, review platforms. AUTHORITY (built over time): published content, third-party citations, AI entity signals. Each tier labeled with control level: full control / partial control / influence only. Bold callout: "Businesses with owned infrastructure generate 2× more revenue than those with social-only presence." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Digital Sovereignty — The Spectrum from Rented to Owned." Horizontal spectrum showing four stages from fully rented to fully sovereign. For each: what discovery looks like, what a platform suspension does to lead volume. Bold callout: "AI citation is the most sovereign discovery channel available — earned through infrastructure, not platform registration." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "DIY Audit vs Professional Audit — What Each Approach Covers." Comparison table with checkmarks and X marks across 10 dimensions. Bold callout: "The highest-leverage gaps are the ones free tools don't find." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Before You Run Ads — The Visibility Infrastructure Checklist." Three tiers: FOUNDATION (website speed, GBP complete, NAP consistent, 10+ reviews), TRUST (photos, review responses, schema markup, FAQ content), AI LAYER (ChatGPT visibility, structured bio, citable content). Each item marked as Critical / Important / Advantage. Bottom callout: "Businesses in the top 10% of conversion rates earn 11.45%+ — at zero additional ad cost." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Free Tools vs Professional Audit — What Each One Covers." Comparison table across 10 dimensions. Bold callout: "Free tools detect errors. Professional audits find what's missing — and what's missing is usually the bigger problem." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The AI Search Alphabet — Plain-English Decoder." Five rows: SEO (Google blue-link rankings — still essential — does not address AI answers), AEO (Google featured snippets — valuable for zero-click — foundational for AI), GEO (AI platform citations — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews — primary 2026 discipline), AIO (umbrella term — not a distinct discipline), LLMO (technical GEO framing — LLM-specific implementation). Bottom: "The outcome is what matters: does your business appear in AI-generated recommendations? That is the question all of these disciplines are trying to answer." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "GEO vs SEO vs AEO — What Each One Optimizes For." Three-column comparison table. SEO: keyword rankings, backlinks, technical crawlability, Google blue links. AEO: featured snippets, FAQ schema, question-answer content, zero-click answers. GEO: schema markup, entity consistency, content citability, AI platform citations. Bottom: "Only 12% of AI citations come from Google's top-ranked pages. The three disciplines require three different strategies." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Digital Audit vs Google Ads — The Sequence That Determines ROI." Flow diagram showing two paths. PATH 1 (wrong order): Ads → Traffic → Low conversion → Wasted spend → Audit too late. PATH 2 (right order): Audit → Fix infrastructure → Ads → Traffic → Higher conversion → ROI. Bold callout: "30–50% of small business ad spend is wasted on traffic arriving at infrastructure that can't convert it." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "GBP Suspension: What the Numbers Say." Five data points displayed as callout cards: (1) 80%+ increase in GBP suspensions, Q1 2023–Q2 2024; (2) 61% of suspended businesses lost measurable leads; (3) Appeal resolution: 5 days → 5 weeks; (4) 42% of suspensions: address verification failures; (5) Businesses with owned website fallback: resumed inquiries within days. Bold callout: "More GBP suspensions occurred last year than in the previous 15 years combined." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "From Link to Answer: What AI Search Requires." A five-step ladder graphic, each step labeled with a building block: (1) Schema markup — machine-readable identity; (2) FAQ content — questions AI can cite; (3) NAP consistency — entity clarity across platforms; (4) Third-party citations — off-site confidence signals; (5) Fresh, authoritative content — recency and expertise. Each step notes the approximate AI citation boost it provides. Caption at the top of the ladder: "The Answer." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Fix Your Online Presence in 30 Days — The Sequence." Four-week breakdown with key actions per week. Week 1: Claim GBP, standardize NAP, submit sitemap. Week 2: LocalBusiness schema, FAQ schema, check robot access. Week 3: Top 3 directories, respond to reviews, social profile audit. Week 4: FAQ page, update service page, run AI visibility test. Each week has a "Why this week" note explaining the build-on logic. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What Gets a Business Into the Google Maps 3-Pack." Three-column structure representing Google's three ranking pillars: RELEVANCE (Primary GBP category, services listed, keyword match), DISTANCE (Business proximity to searcher, service area configuration), PROMINENCE (Review volume and recency, website authority, NAP consistency, citation quality, GBP completeness). Each column has a key action item below it. Bold callout at bottom: "8 of the top 10 ranking signals come directly from the Google Business Profile." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "How to Read Your AI Citation Report in 15 Minutes." Two sections. TOP: "Five Queries to Run" — listed with brief descriptions. BOTTOM: "Five Things to Check in Every Response" — Accuracy of facts; Completeness vs. competitors; Source attribution; Sentiment and framing; Presence or absence. Each item with a one-line interpretation guide. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "How to Test Your AI Visibility in 30 Minutes." Four-step visual: Step 1 — Write 5 queries your customers actually use; Step 2 — Open ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google in incognito; Step 3 — Run each query twice and document results; Step 4 — Calculate visibility score: (appearances ÷ total tests) × 100. Below the steps: a scoring guide — Below 10% = AI-invisible; 10–50% = partial visibility; Above 50% = strong foundation. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Visual Identity in the Age of AI — What Machines Are Processing." Three columns: (1) What AI sees — profile photos, brand color consistency, image metadata, visual entity signals across platforms; (2) What it means — consistent visual brand = stronger entity recognition = more confident AI citations; (3) What to do — professional headshot audit, LinkedIn photo review, color palette consistency check, digital brand alignment. Caption: "Your image is data. In 2026, it's being processed at machine speed." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Google Indexing vs. AI Trust — Two Different Standards." Two-column comparison table. LEFT (Google Indexing): What it measures = page crawlability; Key factors = keywords, backlinks, domain age; Conversion rate = 1.23%; Result = ranked in search results. RIGHT (AI Trust): What it measures = recommendation confidence; Key factors = schema, NAP consistency, third-party citations, content citability; Conversion rate = 3.6%; Result = recommended in AI responses. Bold callout below: "Only 12% of AI citations come from Google's top-10 results." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Industry-Specific AI Visibility Signals — What Actually Matters by Vertical." Five-column layout with industry icons at top. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES: Credential directories, Association listings, License schema. HEALTHCARE: Specialty directories, Healthcare schema, Insurance signals. LOCAL SERVICES: Foursquare, GBP, Data aggregators. REAL ESTATE: Portal profiles, Response speed, Lead capture. PERSONAL BRAND: Person schema, Entity specificity, Original content. Bottom: "A generic audit applies the same rubric to all of them. An industry-tailored audit applies the right one." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Med Spa Local SEO Audit — 12 Points That Determine Your Patient Acquisition Rate." 12 numbered rows organized in three groups: FOUNDATION (GBP, NAP, schema), VISIBILITY (AI test, directories, reviews), CONVERSION (content, intake, after-hours, mobile). Each row has a "% impact on new patients" callout. Bottom stat: "Med spas in the local 3-pack capture 40–60% of 'near me' search clicks." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The Quarterly NAP Audit — What to Check and Where." Left column: "Your Canonical NAP" — a box where the business records its official name, address, and phone format. Right column: 10 platform rows with status indicators (consistent / inconsistent): Website, Google Business Profile, Yelp, Facebook, Apple Maps, Bing Places, BBB, Industry Directory 1, Industry Directory 2, Data Aggregators. Bold callout: "Run this every quarter. Takes under an hour. Inconsistencies compound for years if ignored." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "One-Time Audit vs Ongoing Monitoring — What Each One Does." Two-column layout. ONE-TIME AUDIT: point-in-time diagnostic, establishes baseline, identifies what is broken, produces action plan. ONGOING MONITORING: detects when infrastructure drifts, tracks GBP changes, catches AI citation shifts, monitors competitor movement. Arrow: "The correct sequence: audit first → implement fixes → monitor to protect the gains." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SEO Audit vs Online Presence Audit — What Each One Checks." Checklist comparison table with checkmarks and X marks for both audit types across 10 dimensions. Bold callout: "Most businesses commission an SEO audit thinking they're getting both. Here is what the SEO audit doesn't see." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Organic Search vs AI Citations — Lead Quality Comparison." Two-column layout. ORGANIC SEARCH: high volume, early consideration stage, keyword intent, 1.76% average conversion, requires sorting for qualification. AI CITATIONS: lower volume, late consideration stage, pre-qualified intent, 4.4× conversion premium, arrive with context complete. Bold callout: "AI-referred visitors convert at 4.4× the rate of organic search visitors. Only 12% of AI citations overlap with Google's top-10 results." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The First-Responder Advantage in Real Estate." Three-section layout: TOP: The problem — 78% of leads go to first responder; average agent response time: 917 minutes; agents responding in 5 min are 21× more likely to qualify. MIDDLE: The cost — one missed after-hours lead per week at $20K average commission = $1M/year in lost pipeline. BOTTOM: The fix — AI voice agent ($400–$800/mo) answers immediately at any hour; ROI from one recovered transaction covers 6+ months of cost. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Google Penalty & Suspension Recovery — The Correct Sequence." Three-column layout by event type: MANUAL ACTION (Search Console → resolve violation → reconsideration request → wait), ALGORITHMIC (diagnose cause → improve quality → wait for next update cycle), GBP SUSPENSION (gather exact documentation → submit appeal → do not create new profile → follow up). Bottom row: "Do not take: speculative changes, new profile creation, premature reconsideration requests." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Why Googling Your Own Business Gives You Fake Rankings." Four reasons listed as callout cards: (1) Google personalizes results based on your location, history, and account; (2) Incognito removes your history but not your location; (3) Your non-clicks lower your own CTR signal; (4) Competitor rankings look different from where your customers are searching. Bottom: "What to use instead: Google Search Console, rank-tracking tools, AI platform tests, and a friend's phone." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs Semrush vs Ahrefs — What Each One Actually Checks." Coverage comparison table with 9 dimensions and checkmark/X notation. Bold callout: "Semrush and Ahrefs audit the website. SX Audits audits the full digital presence." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs GustyAudit — Where in the Funnel Each One Works." Funnel diagram: DISCOVERY (AI platforms, GBP, NAP, schema) → ARRIVAL (website traffic) → CONVERSION (UX, friction, CTA). SX Audits addresses the discovery layer. GustyAudit addresses the conversion layer. Bold callout: "AI-referred visitors convert at 4.4× the rate of organic traffic. Establish discovery first, then optimize conversion." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs NordicDigi — What Each One Delivers." Comparison table with 8 dimensions. Bold callout: "A web agency builds the asset. A digital audit ensures the asset is configured to be found, cited, and recommended." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs RW Ads — What Each One Does." Service type comparison with 8 dimensions. Bold callout: "Strategy built on unverified infrastructure underperforms. Infrastructure diagnosis comes first." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs SEO Agency — What Each One Is Built to Do." Quick comparison table with six dimensions. Bold callout: "Fewer than 12% of SEO agency teams have a GEO strategy. Only 12% of AI citations overlap with Google's top-10 organic results." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "SX Audits vs Zephora Consulting — Specialist vs Generalist." Service scope comparison with 8 dimensions. Bold callout: "A digital audit from a firm that sells 15 services is not the same as a digital audit from a firm whose only product is the audit." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Voice Agent Compatibility — What the Audit Checks." Three-component breakdown: Information Accuracy (GBP, FAQ content), Content Accessibility (structure for AI access), Integration Readiness (calendar, booking system). Bold callout: "The same schema that earns AI citations supports AI voice accuracy. Configure both before deploying either." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The 5 Things AI Verifies Before Recommending Your Business." Five scored rows in a scoring table format. Each row shows the dimension, its weight (points), a "PASS" example, and a "FAIL" example. Total possible score: 100. Bold callout: "A business scoring below 60 is unlikely to appear in AI recommendations for competitive queries." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The 6 Things an AI Visibility Audit Actually Checks." Six numbered rows in a vertical list, each with a percentage weight or point value and a one-sentence description: (1) Technical Crawlability — 20 pts — Can AI bots reach and read your content? (2) Entity Recognition & Schema — 20 pts — Is your business clearly defined for AI systems? (3) Content Citation Readiness — 30 pts — Does your content give AI something to quote? (4) NAP Consistency — 15 pts — Is your information identical everywhere it appears? (5) Third-Party Validation — 10 pts — Do authoritative sources mention you? (6) Platform Testing — Direct queries across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding at bottom.

Titled "How AI Evaluates a Business Before Recommending It." Five rows, each with an icon and a pass/fail example. (1) NAP Consistency — PASS: identical across all platforms / FAIL: 3 different phone numbers found. (2) GBP Status — PASS: claimed, verified, complete / FAIL: unclaimed, no hours listed. (3) Schema Markup — PASS: LocalBusiness schema present / FAIL: no structured data. (4) Content to Cite — PASS: FAQ and service pages present / FAIL: only a homepage and contact page. (5) Third-Party Mentions — PASS: 12 authoritative citations / FAIL: 0 off-site mentions. Bold callout: "AI skips businesses that fail even two of these." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The 30-Day Post-Audit Implementation Sequence." Four-week calendar view: WEEK 1 (foundation: schema, GBP, top NAP fixes), WEEK 2 (schema layer: FAQ schema, sameAs links, validation), WEEK 3 (citation authority: directories, aggregators, one citation), WEEK 4 (content: About page rewrite, FAQ content, freshness). DAY 60–90: Follow-up audit. Bottom callout: "Most high-impact fixes are one-time actions, not ongoing campaigns." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Vertical infographic titled "What a Digital Audit Actually Covers." Six numbered rows, each with an icon, category label, and one-line description: (1) Website & Technical — schema, speed, metadata; (2) Brand & NAP Consistency — name, address, phone across all platforms; (3) Local SEO & AI Visibility — Google, ChatGPT, Perplexity; (4) Social Media Infrastructure — linked correctly, feeding authority; (5) Systems & Intake — calls, forms, after-hours capture; (6) AI Readiness — voice agents, automation gaps. Dark background, gold accent lines, Sovereign X branding at the bottom.

Titled "SEO vs. AEO vs. GEO — What Each One Actually Targets." A three-row comparison table with columns: Discipline / What It Targets / What You Need / Who's Missing It. Row 1: SEO — Google blue links — keywords, backlinks, domain authority — businesses ignoring AI. Row 2: AEO — Featured snippets, zero-click answers — FAQ structure, direct answers — most small businesses. Row 3: GEO — ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews — schema, citations, entity clarity — 88%+ of businesses. Dark background, gold accent lines, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "AI Readiness for Small Businesses — What It Measures." Three-tier pyramid structure. Foundation (bottom): GBP claimed, NAP consistent, schema implemented, FAQ content present. Intermediate (middle): Directory listings, third-party mentions, content freshness. Advanced (top): llms.txt, citation monitoring, competitive benchmarking. Side callout: "Most businesses are not yet at the foundation tier. Start there." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "How an AI Readiness Score Is Calculated." Five horizontal score bars, each labeled with a dimension name, its weight, and a fill level showing a typical underperforming business: Technical Access (20 pts) — 12/20; Entity Clarity (20 pts) — 8/20; Content Readiness (30 pts) — 5/30; Third-Party Validation (20 pts) — 4/20; Freshness (10 pts) — 3/10. Total shown: 32/100. Bold callout: "Above 70 = AI-ready. Below 30 = AI-invisible." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Online Presence vs. Having a Website." Two columns side by side. LEFT: "A Website" — one URL, one touchpoint, invisible without traffic, zero authority on its own. RIGHT: "An Online Presence" — GBP, directories, reviews, social signals, schema markup, AI citations, NAP consistency across all platforms. Below both columns: "Most businesses have the left. Their competitors are building the right." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding at bottom.

Titled "The 5 Dimensions of an AI Readiness Audit." Five rows with icons: (1) AI Platform Testing — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, 5 query types, consistency testing; (2) Schema Markup — LocalBusiness, FAQ, Person, sameAs links, Rich Results validation; (3) NAP Consistency — 30+ directories, data aggregators, severity scoring; (4) Content Citability — structured bio, FAQ content, heading organization, freshness, original perspective content; (5) Trust Signals — third-party citations, review profile, response pattern. Score range: 0–100. AI-ready threshold: 70+. Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "The Living Blog Audit — What It Finds and What to Do." Three-category content sorting: Optimize (structural improvements → AI citation eligibility), Consolidate (merge → concentrate authority), Remove (remove → restore domain authority). Bold callout: "Pages not updated quarterly are 3× more likely to lose AI citation rates." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What Is llms.txt — and Should You Have One?" Three-row layout: (1) What it is — a plain-text file guiding AI systems to your most important content; (2) Current adoption — 3.2% of websites have one; no major AI company has publicly committed to reading it yet; (3) Priority order for small businesses — Schema markup first → NAP consistency → GBP → FAQ content → llms.txt. Bold callout: "30 minutes to implement. Low risk. High upside as AI crawler adoption grows." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What Schema Markup Does for Your Business." Four-section layout: (1) What it is — structured data code embedded in your website HTML; (2) What it does — tells AI and search engines your business identity explicitly; (3) The results — 20–30% higher CTR, rich results, AI citation eligibility; (4) How to check — Google Rich Results Test URL. Bold callout: "Two hours of work. Years of compounding return." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Who Tells Your Story If You Don't." Four panels, each showing a different force filling the narrative vacuum: (1) Review platforms — star ratings and individual reviews, indexed permanently; (2) AI systems — summaries built from whatever structured data is available; (3) Competitors — appearing in recommendations where you're absent; (4) Time — outdated content that remains visible years after it was accurate. Below all four: "Owned narrative infrastructure replaces all four with your voice." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "What Most Digital Audits Miss — The Five Suppression Dimensions." Five panels: AI platform visibility, GBP accuracy, NAP consistency, schema markup, trust signals — each with a brief description of what the gap costs and why standard audits don't check it. Bold callout: "These five dimensions are what determine whether a prospective client finds, trusts, and contacts your business in 2026." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Where Revenue Leaks in a Digital Presence." Five leak types illustrated: AI platform absence, GBP errors, NAP inconsistency, AI Overview exclusion, trust signal gaps. Revenue impact estimates for each. Bold callout: "Businesses lose 20–40% of potential revenue to preventable digital infrastructure gaps." Dark background, gold accents, Sovereign X branding.

Titled "Google Removed Your Business — The Recovery Sequence."
